slot.brief: For PCl5 ⇌ PCl3 + Cl2 at total equilibrium pressure P and degree of dissociation α, derive Kp; numerical with given α or given Kp to find α.

stem: A $0.100$ molal solution of $\text{CoCl}_3\cdot x\text{NH}_3$ has $\Delta T_f=0.465$ K; take $K_f=1.86\ \text{K kg mol}^{-1}$. If $0.75$ of the formula units ionise, find $x$. Co(III) has coordination number 6, and only outer-sphere chloride ions ionise.

verdicts.working: Calculate the van’t Hoff factor: i = 0.465/(1.86 × 0.100) = 2.5. With x − 3 outer-sphere chlorides, ionisation yields x − 2 particles. Thus 2.5 = 1 + 0.75[(x − 2) − 1], giving x = 5.

working:
$i=\dfrac{\Delta T_f}{K_fm}=\dfrac{0.465}{1.86\times0.100}=2.50$
If $n$ chloride ions are outside the coordination sphere, $i=1+n\alpha$.
$n=\dfrac{2.50-1}{0.75}=2$.
Thus one chloride is coordinated; $x+1=6\Rightarrow x=5$.

Independent check: Calculate the van’t Hoff factor: i = 0.465/(1.86 × 0.100) = 2.5. With x − 3 outer-sphere chlorides, ionisation yields x − 2 particles. Thus 2.5 = 1 + 0.75[(x − 2) − 1], giving x = 5.
solution:
$i=\dfrac{\Delta T_f}{K_fm}=\dfrac{0.465}{1.86\times0.100}=2.50$.
For $n$ outer-sphere chloride ions, $i=1+n\alpha$, so $n=\dfrac{2.50-1}{0.75}=2$.
Thus one chloride is coordinated; with coordination number $6$, $x+1=6$, giving $x=5$.
